target_customer: Musicians, festivals, events and creators (over 10,000 per the company) who pay a monthly subscription plus messaging fees
problem: Artists depend on platforms they do not own to reach fans around releases and ticket or merch drops; Laylo captures fan contacts and sends drop notifications by SMS, email and Instagram DM.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription (premium from $25 per month) plus usage-based messaging
product_category: Fan CRM and drop marketing platform for music and events

founders.name: Alec Ellin
founders.background_notes: Background from Built In LA (2019-10-03). Education not found.

investors: Sony Music Entertainment (lead, per Crunchbase as cited by Built In LA)

competitors.name: Spotify for Artists
competitors.what: Artist dashboards and analytics that Laylo's approach contrasts with

competitors.name: SoundCloud
competitors.what: Artist dashboard and distribution platform named alongside Spotify

technical_complexity.rationale: Landing pages, messaging via SMS, email and Instagram, and link tracking are standard SaaS integrations; the harder parts are messaging deliverability and platform APIs.

defensibility.rationale: Artists' fan lists and drop history create switching cost, but presave, link and messaging tools such as feature.fm, Linkfire and Hypeddit offer overlapping features.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Laylo depends on Instagram and Spotify integrations (platform dependency risk) and no incumbent was found acquiring or copying it; it added Spotify presaves in August 2023.

market_need_then: In 2019 Ellin said Laylo would hit revenue targets almost a year early and expected a partnership giving access to tens of thousands of artists (Built In LA, 2019-10-03); artists lacked owned audiences.

identity.visual_style: Music and culture oriented, drop pages
identity.voice_and_tone: Hype oriented headlines such as 'Capture every fan, crush every drop'

branding.brand_signature: The astronaut helmet logo and the term drops
branding.community_and_virality: Used by artists including Diplo, HAIM, Sabrina Carpenter and Rosalia per its site logos; company claims over $1B revenue and 150M+ fan interactions generated for customers.

brand_strength.rationale: Strong recognition inside the music and events industry via artist customers and label partners; no evidence of consumer-level brand pull, and the helmet and name origins are not explained.

pivots.from: Technology that tracks how music spreads online
pivots.to: Fan notification and CRM platform for artists
pivots.why: Built In LA (2019) says Laylo began by tracking music spread; the notification product followed

outcome_analysis: Laylo raised a $1.5M seed in 2019, a Eldridge-led strategic round in 2021 and another in October 2022 for about $8M total, and became a CRM used by major artists and events with label and agency partners, adding AI agents in 2026. It stayed small (24 team members) and venture funding was modest, so growth appears driven by artist adoption rather than large capital.
notes: The 2021 amount of about $3M appears only in an LA Business Journal snippet (labelled seed there); the BusinessWire release itself could not be fetched (403), so the stage is other and total more than $5M comes from search summaries. Total reached $8M after October 2022 per MBW and Tubefilter, the round amount was not stated. A seed from Sony in 2019 relies on Crunchbase as cited by Built In LA. Aggregator figures for 2022 differ (Preqin $3.26M, CB Insights $3M). Launch date is conflicting (Product Hunt October 2020 vs 2021 reports). Competitor list uses the only dated sources found; presave rivals (feature.fm, Linkfire, Hypeddit) come from Laylo's own 2023 blog and are not dated at the batch.
